The 36 Classic changed materially over its long production run. Wood construction continued through mid-1973; later boats are fiberglass. In 1987/1988 the hull grew approximately six inches in length and four to six inches in beam. Single and twin diesel installations both exist.

ResearchNotes: Canadian Tollycruisers reports 887 Tollycraft 26 Sedans built from 1973-1987. HMY/Powerboat Guide reports 26'8" LOA, 10'0" beam, 2'10" draft, 9,000 lb displacement, 10'0" clearance, 140 US gal fuel, 33 US gal water and 10 US gal waste. Window frames were upgraded in 1977 and the interior changed to teak in 1982. Most boats used a single 255 hp gasoline V-drive; B-Atlas therefore leaves plan-critical fuel classification unresolved for individual-boat verification.
